english: Of-True-Fame, how did you hit the oak with your spear? I kept my eye on the oak, and then I threw the spear with a strong arm. Give me the spear, and I will throw it. Stand here, and throw it toward the oak. I threw it, but it fell on the ground. Throw it again; your arm will become strong. Are you tired? I am not tired; I will throw it three times.

english: Son, the sheep came home, but one lamb is missing. I saw all of them in the field, mother. Where did the lamb go? Seek it near the river, for night is coming. I will take the dog with me. The dog smells the lambs. Go now! Are you afraid of the night? I am not afraid; he will be with me.

english: Having heard this, the sheep fled into the plain.

english: Old woman, our calf does not eat; he lies on the ground. Is his belly swelling? It is swelling, and he is in pain. He ate new grass. Give me salt and water. What will you do? I will pour it into his mouth and speak words over him. Will the calf live? He will live. Learn these words: you yourself will heal calves.

english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: Craftsman, what are you making from the oak? I am making a wheel for the new wagon. Why did you choose oak and not birch? Oak is strong; birch breaks. Now bore a hole here. I have bored it! Is the hole big? It is small; bore it again. When will the wheel turn under the wagon? When we have made the second wheel, you will drive the wagon.

english: Herdsman, it is getting dark; where is our village? See the stars above! That bright star stands over our village. I have caught sight of it! Let us walk toward it. Take my hand, and do not fall. Who showed you the stars? An old woman showed them to me when I was a boy. Now I show them to you. Will you remember them? I will remember them.

english: Father, teach me the words of the sacrifice. Son, we call the gods to the feast. Then we pour the butter into the fire. What do we say to the fire? We say this. Agni, eat the butter and give us cattle! Why do we give it to him? Because he carries it to the gods. Now say the words with me. Agni, eat the butter and give us cattle! You remember the words; the gods heard you.

english: Grandmother, the fire on the hearth has become small. What shall I do? Lay dry wood on the embers, and the fire will grow. Now smoke is going up, and the fire is burning! May the fire not die in our house! Our grandmothers kept it. Why do we guard it? The fire is a god; he warms the house. Will you guard it this night? I will guard it, and I will not sleep.

pie: mógʰew h₁éḱwosyo kúHloy h₁épi séds? ne sédm̥. h₁éḱwoybʰos bʰebʰóyh₂h₂e. mē bʰéyh₂s. h₁eǵóh₂ ḱóm pṓlHom démh₂m̥. h₁ésyo gʷriHwéh₂m lm̥bʰdʰí dʰr̥h₃dʰí-kʷe. dʰérh₃m̥. h₁ím twṓys ǵnúbʰis gm̥dʰí pró-kʷe spéḱye. h₂éwh₂e réydʰoh₂. widés me? widóm te. HeHḱúh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ h₂éyeri réydʰēsi.
english: Boy, have you sat on the back of a horse? I have not sat on one. I am afraid of the horses. Do not be afraid! I tamed this foal myself. Grasp his mane and mount! I have mounted! Press him with your knees, and look forward! Grandfather, I am riding! Did you see me? I saw you. Tomorrow you will ride the swift horse.

pie: dʰh₂bʰre h₂éyos ḱósmi dinóy kélh₂oh₂? h₁íd mē kélh₂s. ǵʰésorn̥s moy spéḱye. h₂éyos ph₂wéni topéyoh₂. nu h₁íd soksóy gʷʰn̥sḱési? h₁íd gʷʰn̥sḱóh₂. nu ḱéstrom h₁ésmōd dʰinéǵʰmi. péh₂wr̥ toy ǵʰésorn̥s ne dʰégʷʰeti? h₁yód h₁eǵóh₂ h₂yuHn̥ḱós h₁ésm̥ h₁éwset me. nu moy ǵʰésores soksṓy somHéh₂es. dʰh₂bʰrós éti h₁ésesi? dʰh₂bʰrós h₁ésoh₂ ḱéstreh₂-kʷe wérǵoh₂.
english: Smith, shall I strike the bronze today? Do not strike it! Look at my hands. I heat the bronze in the fire. Then do you strike it on the stone? I strike it. Then I shape a knife from it. Does the fire not burn your hands? When I was young, it burned me. Now my hands are like stone. Will you too be a smith? I will be a smith, and I will make knives.

pie: kʷóti káprōs mógʰew gʰórtoy h₁sénti? septḿ̥ káprōs gʰórtoy h₁sénti. déḱm̥ káprōs dʰǵʰyés h₁idʰé sth₂éh₁yont. kʷóti káprōs lelikʷḗr? tréyes káprōs lelikʷḗr. tóns h₂éǵroy h₂isḱṓh₂? tóns h₂isḱé twóm-kʷe bʰréh₂term̥ sl̥h₂gʷdʰí. tóns widṓmes h₁íns-kʷe dṓm wodʰéyōmes.
english: Boy, how many goats are in the pen? Seven goats are in the pen. Yesterday ten goats stood here. How many goats are missing? Three goats are missing. Shall I seek them in the field? Seek them, and take your brother. We will find them and lead them home.

pie: h₂yúHn̥ḱe te pṓlHos dénḱt. ǵʰésorm̥ moy dénḱt sh₂éymn̥-kʷe léh₁m̥. h₂éǵrom h₂epó drémt. pṓlHōy mē gʰrémes. pṓlHos téḱnōy somHós h₁éwketi-kʷe. kʷíh₁ h₁ím démh₂oh₂? h₁ésmey ǵr̥h₂nóm twéh₂s ǵʰesrés dh₃dʰí. ǵnéh₃eti te. nu me swóy kúHloy h₁épi bʰérēti? bʰérēti te mudrós-kʷe h₁ésesi.
english: Young man, the foal bit you! He bit my hand, and I let go of the rope. He ran away to the field. Do not be angry at the foal. A foal is like a child; he will learn. How shall I tame him? Give him grain from your hand. He will come to know you. Then will he carry me on his back? He will carry you, and you will be glad.

english: Kindly, the wind is blowing, and it is freezing. Snow will fall at dawn. How do you know? The sky is grey, and the birds are silent. Lead the sheep into the pen, and cover the door. Will much snow fall? Much snow will fall, and we will sit by the hearth. Will you tell me a story? I will tell you the story of the serpent!

english: Grandmother, tell me the story of the serpent. The serpent lay around the waters and hid them, and the rivers did not flow. Who slew the serpent? Perkʷunos slew the serpent with his stone. Then he freed them. Shall I tell the story to my sister? Tell it now; I will listen. Perkʷunos slew the serpent and freed the waters. You know the story; your children will hear it from you.

english: King, shall I speak in the assembly? You will speak, but heed the old men. What shall I say to them? Say few words, but true ones. Whoever speaks many words, men do not listen to him. If the old men laugh, I will keep silent. Do not keep silent! A bold word wins fame. Will you be bold? I will be bold, and you will hear my words.

english: Mother-in-law, what shall I cook for the feast? Cook the ram's meat in the big pot. The gods receive the first meat, then the men. Shall I put salt in the pot? Put a little salt and much fat. Did you cook in your mother's house? I cooked mush there, but I did not cook meat. Today you will learn, and the guests will praise you.

english: Brother, look! I see footprints in the snow. Did a dog walk here? A dog did not walk here. A wolf walked here. How do you recognize the wolf's foot? The wolf is bigger than the dog, and his tracks are straight. Shall we follow him? Let us follow him! I will carry the spear. Follow me and keep silent!

english: Sister, the cow is kicking me! Rub her neck, and sing her a song. What shall I sing to the cow? Sing the song of the good cows; she likes it. Now she is standing, and the milk is filling the pot! You have learned. Tomorrow you will milk the cows. Are you tired? I am not tired; I am glad.

english: Smith, what are you melting in the pot? I am melting gold. The king wants a cup of gold. How will you make a cup from the gold? I hollowed out this stone; I will pour the gold into it. Shall I pour it? Do not pour it today; the gold is hot. Be watchful and remember! When will I pour gold? When your arms are strong, you will pour gold for kings.

pie: h₂éwh₂e me h₁éḱwos spr̥néHt. kúdʰe te dʰéwgʰt? skélos moy dʰéwgʰt Hrupyóh₂. h₁ésyo h₁orséh₂m h₁érs. h₁éḱwos tósmōd tréseti h₁yód ne widéh₁yeti. h₁ésyo ḱérh₂sonm̥ gʷm̥sḱé. h₂éti me ne spr̥néHeti? ne te spr̥néHeti wókʷm̥ toy ǵnéh₃eti. éti Hrupyési? Hrupyóh₂ ne HréwdHmi.
english: Uncle, the horse kicked me! Where did he strike you? He struck my leg; I am in pain. You went up to his tail. A horse trembles at what he does not see. Come to his head! Will he not kick me again? He will not kick you; he will come to know your voice. Are you still in pain? I am in pain, but I am not weeping.

pie: swésor pṓlHos kʷsépi ǵn̥h₁yéto. h₁éy ish₁rós stestóh₂e? stestóh₂e h₂mélǵos-kʷe píph₃eti. kʷód h₁némn̥su h₁ésmey dʰéh₁omes? h₁ésmey ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰh₁dʰí h₁yód h₃rēǵés h₁éḱwos h₁éseti. h₁ésmey ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰéh₁oh₂ h₁eǵóh₂-kʷe h₁ím démh₂oh₂. h₁íh₁ éti réydʰōh₂? h₁íh₁ pós réydʰēsi.
english: Sister, a foal was born in the night! Is he strong? Is he standing? He is standing, and he is drinking milk. What name shall we give him? Give him a famous name, for he will be the horse of a king. I will give him a famous name, and I will tame him myself. Shall I ride him too? You will ride him after me!

pie: h₁súḱlewes nos h₂ŕ̥tḱos gʰórdʰom dʰǵʰyés gʷémt. h₁ím kʷéḱs? h₁ím ne kʷéḱm̥ h₁ésyo pédās widóm. h₁ésyo toy pṓds ǵʰóstōd méǵyōs? h₁éy moy ǵʰóstōd méǵyōs. h₁ím wrégēsi? h₁ím ne wrégōmes stéh₂dʰh₁ōm péh₂somes. h₂ŕ̥tḱos tribʰós wiHróybʰos ḱéwh₁yōs. nu tébʰye ḱóm bʰéwdʰōh₂.
english: Of-Good-Fame, yesterday a bear came to our fence. Did you catch sight of him? I did not catch sight of him, but I saw his tracks. Is his foot bigger than your hand? It is bigger than my hand. Will you hunt him? We will not hunt him; we will guard the herd. A bear is stronger than three men. Then I will stay awake with you.

pie: téḱnom snéh₂si? ne snéh₂mi déh₂nu dʰubʰróm. twóy kúHloy l̥gʰdʰí dʰoréyōh₂-kʷe te. nu h₂r̥Hmóns skélesh₂-kʷe Hyowdʰéye. snéh₂mi dʰoréyesi me? ne te dʰoréyoh₂ túH-ge snéh₂si. mogʰúbʰos wéwkēsi? h₁éymos wéwkōh₂ sméyonti-kʷe.
english: Child, do you swim? I do not swim; the river is deep. Lie down on your back, and I will hold you. Now move your arms and your legs. I am swimming! Are you holding me? I am not holding you; you yourself are swimming! Will you tell the boys? I will tell them, and they will laugh.

pie: kʷíd ǵĺ̥h₂ow gʷénh₂es séngʷʰonti h₁yód wiHrós snusóm wédʰeti? ḱód séngʷʰonti snúse nos ḱéyweh₂ h₁sdʰí ḱóymosyo pótnih₂ h₁sdʰí. kʷíd snusós próti mléwHti? ḱód sokʷéyeti ḱéywos wos h₁ésoh₂ h₂éHsh₂m̥-kʷe wos h₂léksōh₂. ḱéywos wos h₁ésoh₂ h₂éHsh₂m̥-kʷe wos h₂léksōh₂. nu nos túH swésōr.
english: Sister-in-law, what do the women sing when a man leads a bride? They sing this: 'Bride, be dear to us; be the mistress of the household!' What does the bride say back? She says this: 'I will be dear to you, and I will guard your hearth.' I will be dear to you, and I will guard your hearth. Now you are our sister.

pie: owis, yesmin wl̥nā ne ēst, dedorḱe eḱwons wogʰom gʷr̥um wegʰontn̥s, bʰorom meǵHm, monum ōḱu bʰerontn̥s.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: ph₂ter wóǵʰom déh₂nu ḱósmi dinóy h₂éǵōh₂. uksénh₁e te ḱlowséyētes? ḱlowséyētes me h₂éǵtreh₂m bʰérōh₂. tóh₁ mē gʷʰn̥sḱés tóybʰos bʰh₂dʰí. spéḱye kʷékʷlōs wértontor. uksénh₁e h₃reǵtóy stóygʰoy wédʰe. déh₂nu h₁ludʰóme. túH mudrós? h₁eǵóh₂ mudrós suHnús moy wóǵʰom h₁élh₂t.
english: Father, today I will drive the wagon to the river! Will the oxen heed you? They will heed me; I will carry the goad. Do not strike them; speak to them. Look, the wheels are turning! Lead the oxen along the straight path. We have reached the river! Are you glad? I am glad: my son drove the wagon.
